title: Swedish meatballs with cream or white sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Swedish meatballs are small balls made from ground meat (usually a mix of beef and pork), seasoned with spices and onion. They are served with a smooth cream or white sauce made from stock, flour and cream. The dish is a staple of Scandinavian cuisine and is found on menus worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic Swedish recipe was first recorded in cookbooks in the 19th century.
In Sweden the meatballs are traditionally accompanied by lingonberry jam and mashed potatoes.
The cream sauce (sås) can be light or thicker depending on the amount of flour and cream used.
Original recipes use a 2:1 ratio of beef to pork.
Meatballs are often steamed before frying to keep them juicy.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Meatballs provide complete animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat is rich in B12, B6 and niacin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health and blood formation.

items.title: Calcium from the sauce
items.content: The cream‑based sauce adds calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The dish is suitable for low‑carb diets, as most carbohydrates come from the sauce, which can be adjusted.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Cream and meat can raise saturated fat intake, so people with heart disease should limit portions.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt is added for flavor; excessive sodium may increase blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cream sauce contains milk, which can trigger reactions in those with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking of the meat mixture can allow pathogens such as Salmonella to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the meatballs hot, drizzled with the cream or white sauce. They are commonly paired with mashed potatoes, boiled vegetables or lingonberry jam. They can also be tossed with pasta or used in casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked meatballs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store the sauce separately. For longer keeping, freeze in bags for 2‑3 months; thaw completely and reheat before serving.
